A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to build a Byzantine-toleran machine learning system that is secure and efficient.

Krum is a Byzantine-tolerated SGD aggregation rule that can be implemented with a constant factor overhead in the communication and computation complexity, and with no additional communication rounds.
we provide the first algorithm for distributed learning that is resilient to Byzantine adversaries, while preserving the convergence guarantees of the standard SGD algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Byzantine resilience can be achieved in distributed machine learning without sacrificing accuracy.
the Byzantine-tolerated learning problem is not only theoretically feasible, but also practical, and that the Byzantine problem in learning is not as hard as previously thought.
the Byzantine fault model, which was originally developed for the context of distributed computing, is applicable also to machine learning.
